mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and Apostilled or consular-legalized, as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, limited partners above the 25% threshold, senior managers and authorized representatives against the Canadian Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Criminal Code Part II.1 terrorist group lists, the US OFAC SDN List, and Her Majesty's Treasury sanctions where relevant. Enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth and source of funds, applies to all domestic and foreign politically-exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of state, senior public office holders, judiciary, senior military officers and heads of state-owned enterprises. Any potential sanctions/terrorism match requires immediate escalation and filing of a suspicious transaction report to FINTRAC; no investment is accepted until unresolved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ServiceOntario Ontario Business Registry (for limited partnerships under the laws of the Province of Ontario), using the National Unified Automated Name Search (NUANS) via an authorized agent; federal trademark name clearance through the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate/partnership name must be in English, French, or both, and expressed in Roman script. Non-Latin script names must be submitted with an official transliteration into English or French. In Quebec, a French version is mandatory. The name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element, e.g., 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 's.e.n.c.' where applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives written reasons. Within 30 days, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Director of Companies/Registrar under the applicable Limited Partnership Act. The Director issues a written decision within 60 days; a further judicial review application lies to the superior court of the province, or to the Federal Court for federal matters. Alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a fresh name request with an amended NUANS search at any time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are acceptable for the registered office address and service-of-process address. However, for ISIC 3250 / NAICS 334510 (multi-parameter bedside telemetry monitor assembly and calibration), a physical operational site in Canada is mandatory to satisfy Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL), ISO 13485, and commercial substance expectations of the CRA. A virtual office alone is not a substitute for the physical manufacturing/calibration facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85.0% likelihood of an announced or unannounced Health Canada establishment inspection within the first 18 months of registration, and elevated CRA tax audit probability if input tax credits or scientific research claims are made.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5-12 and Sch. I (governance framework); Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (flow-through partnership taxation); provincial Limited Partnerships Act applicable at the registered office, with federal-coordinated extra-provincial registration under the CBCA framework.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), in coordination with the provincial Corporate Registry constituting the limited partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership / Certificate of Limited Partnership, together with Extra-Provincial Registration Form Form 10 where operations extend beyond the registration province
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Canadian limited partnership; initial capital contributions are fixed in the Limited Partnership Agreement and may be held in escrow pending issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership. All partners remain subject to anti-money-laundering verification under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the General Partner of the Limited Partnership, as follows: 1. That the capital contributions subscribed by the initial Limited Partners, as set out in Schedule A, be accepted and paid into the partnership's escrow account pending issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership. 2. That the registered office of the Limited Partnership be established at the address recorded with the registry, and that the registered agent be authorized to receive process. 3. That [Name] be appointed General Partner and [Name] appointed Chief Financial and Compliance Officer, each with authority to open banking arrangements, execute filings, and complete the formation docket.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre — Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) through a registered search provider to confirm the limited partnership name is distinctive, not confusingly similar, and contains the required legal element (Limited, Ltee, or L.P.); file the name reservation online through ISED and secure a 90-day reservation.
required_dossiers: Applicant authorization letter
NUANS name search report
Proposed name with legal element (L.P. / Limited)
Consent of any named individual or entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name designation is refused, file a written reconsideration submission with ISED or select a revised distinctive name and re-file within the remaining reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and executing witnesses (notarization not statutorily mandated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement covering capital contributions, profit and loss allocation ratios, distribution waterfall, management authority of the general partner, transfer restrictions, and dissolution triggers; execute in counterpart by all general and limited partners, with signatures witnessed.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (executed counterpart)
Schedule A: initial capital contribution schedule
Beneficial ownership register (PCMLTFA verification)
Power of attorney records for non-resident partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the governance terms, file a supplemental confirmation letter and restated contribution schedule signed by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration / Certificate of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Corporate Registry (federal-coordinated CA-FED filing window through Corporations Canada)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Declaration of Limited Partnership, stating the registered office address in Canada, name and address of the registered agent, full legal names of all general partners, and the date of commencement; pay the prescribed filing fee electronically and obtain a certified Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Limited Partnership
NUANS name approval certificate
Consent to act of registered agent
Proof of registered office address (lease or letter of direction)
General partner resolutions (wet-ink or e-signed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is refused for a defect, file an Amended Declaration within 15 days curing the noted deficiency; retroactive effective dates will not be accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with the CRA to obtain a nine-digit Business Number; open the GST/HST account (mandatory where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), payroll account, and confirm the flow-through partnership classification for T5013 reporting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Partners' identification (SIN or BN) and residential status
Authorization of the general partner as primary contact
Bank account details for CRA direct debit and refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA flags beneficial ownership or residential-status mismatches, submit corrected ownership schedules with a written explanation within 30 days of the query letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Bank Account and Capital Funding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank in Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a business bank account in the exact legal name of the limited partnership; execute an escrow agreement whereby initial capital contributions remain blocked until issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership and the first board resolution; release funds to the operating account upon satisfaction of all conditions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
First board resolution appointing signing officers
Beneficial ownership and politically exposed person verification forms
Bank account mandate and specimen signatures
Escrow agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, deliver updated registry extracts, an organizational chart, and certified copies of the partnership agreement within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration (if operating outside the registration province)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registries of the target Canadian provinces and territories
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Registration in each jurisdiction where the partnership carries on business; appoint an attorney for service of process in each province; obtain the extra-provincial certificate before commencing operations in that province.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificate of Limited Partnership
Extra-provincial registration application form
Consent of attorney for service
Certificate of existence or status from the home registry
Provincial filing fee payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a province rejects the partnership name, file an assumed-name certificate and re-register under the alternate name within ten days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Registered Agent, and Partnership Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and corporate record provider in Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the registered office at a physical address in the jurisdiction, appoint the registered agent, and maintain the partnership minute book containing the certificate, partnership agreement, register of partners, capital ledger, consents of officers, and meeting records; keep the office accessible during normal business hours for service of process.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Register of partners with contribution schedule
Consent of registered agent to act
Governance by-laws of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or a bank rejects the record pack for want of seal or notarization, provide certified and apostilled copies within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Taxpayer Services and T5013 Processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a fiscal year-end (default December 31) and configure the T5013 partnership information return; issue T5013 slips to each partner reflecting their allocable share of income and file the T5013 Summary with the CRA; file Form T1139 where a non-calendar fiscal period is adopted.
required_dossiers: CRA Business Number confirmation
Partnership identification form
Complete partner list with allocation percentages
Financial statements and capital account roll-forwards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA assesses a late-filing penalty, submit a taxpayer relief application with mitigating facts and corrected schedules within 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Health Canada — Medical Devices Directorate (MDEL online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the medical device establishment licence application; classify the multi-parameter ECG telemetry monitor as a Class II device under the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282); provide ISO 13485 or MDSAP certification evidence, device labelling under IEC 60601-1 and CSA C22.2, and a site master file; pay the annual MDEL fee.
required_dossiers: MDEL application form with fee schedule
ISO 13485 or MDSAP certificate
Device classification statement under SOR/98-282 Schedule 1
Site master file and quality manual
Labelling compliance declarations (IEC 60601-1 / CSA C22.2 No. 60601-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Health Canada issues a deficiency letter, respond within 30 days with the requested quality and labelling evidence; escalate to the Directorate for reconsideration if the deficiency is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environment and Climate Change Canada; provincial fire marshal; provincial occupational health and safety authority; Electrical Safety Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the facility under applicable environmental reporting programs; obtain fire safety certification reflecting National Building Code of Canada Part 3 compliance; secure a structural load inspection certificate; obtain occupational health and safety clearance and register with the provincial workers' compensation board before commencing calibration operations.
required_dossiers: Environmental compliance registration (CEPA Schedule), if applicable
Fire marshal inspection certificate
Structural load inspection report
Workplace OHS clearance and workers' compensation board registration
Electrical Safety Authority inspection certificate for the calibration laboratory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any clearance is withheld, complete the corrective action notice, arrange re-inspection, and appeal through the provincial administrative tribunal within the statutory appeal window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) issued under the Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) in coordination with the provincial environmental protection agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Environmental Screening Registration; no full EIA is required for low-impact electronics and calibration assembly, but a full EIA is triggered where solvent throughput exceeds CEPA VOC thresholds or hazardous waste generation exceeds provincial registration limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Fisheries Act, s. 36(3) deleterious-substance prohibition and municipal sewer bylaws (pH 6.0-9.0; total suspended solids <= 350 mg/L); VOCs: <= 10 tonnes/year per single substance and <= 20 tonnes/year aggregate under CEPA; electronic waste: waste destined to authorized recyclers; lead (TCLP) <= 5 mg/L; no ozone-depleting substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per National Building Code of Canada (NBC) Part 3 covering sprinkler, egress, and compartmentation requirements; structural load inspection certificate for the assembly and calibration floor; occupational health and safety clearance under the applicable provincial OHS Act including WHMIS/GHS hazard communication, electrical safety inspection of ECG calibration equipment per CSA C22.2, and registration with the provincial workers' compensation board.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — My Business Account digital portal, GST/HST NETFILE, and the CRA Partnership Information Return (T5013) system; customs program account ('RD') is administered jointly with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership under the applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act (non-resident general partner must appoint an attorney for service in the province of registration; e.g., Form LP2A in Ontario). Step 2: Apply to CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) in the LP's legal name using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number); non-resident applicants file Form RC1A. Step 3: Add program accounts to the BN: 'RC' for GST/HST registration, 'RM' for payroll (if the LP has employees), and 'RD' for import/export transactions via CBSA. Step 4: The partnership itself is required to file an annual T5013 information return if it carries on business in Canada and has a corporate partner or a partner that is a non-resident. Step 5: Each partner independently obtains or maintains its own tax identification number for reporting its allocated share of LP income in its home jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — fiscally transparent under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act; the LP computes income at partnership level and allocates to partners for taxation in their own hands. The LP is nonetheless a distinct 'person' registered for GST/HST under the Excise Tax Act. A non-resident partner is taxable in Canada under Part I on its share of Canadian-source business income and may also be subject to Part XIII withholding on any interest, rent, or royalty payments sourced in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Subsection 249.1(5) election to adopt a non-calendar partnership taxation year. 2) Subsection 96(3)/(3.1) partnership agreement on income and loss allocation, binding on all partners and acceptable to CRA. 3) Section 156 Excise Tax Act election whereby a registrant partner that controls the partnership elects, jointly with the LP, to treat otherwise taxable supplies between them as made for nil consideration. 4) Subsection 18.4(4) Income Tax Act election, applicable where the Canadian LP is treated as an opaque corporation under a foreign tax system, to deem the partnership a corporation solely for Canada's hybrid mismatch regime compliance. 5) Subsection 152(4) waiver election to extend the CRA reassessment period beyond the normal four-year window.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Harmonized Sales Tax (HST), Parts IX and X of the Excise Tax Act, administered by CRA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD — GST/HST small-supplier threshold determined by taxable supplies made in Canada during the preceding four calendar quarters; a non-resident LP exceeding this threshold must register. Voluntary registration is available regardless of revenue to recover input tax credits on export-related and pre-operating expenses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or mandatory digital stamping exists in Canada. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records if the format permits verification and data extraction in English or French. Canada participates voluntarily in the Peppol pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework for B2B transactions. GST/HST registrants must retain complete invoice and export evidence pursuant to section 286 of the Excise Tax Act; failure to maintain adequate electronic or paper records is itself an offence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of multi-parameter ECG bedside telemetry monitors and subcontracted calibration services qualify for 0% GST/HST if the goods are exported in the ordinary course of business (section 6, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act) or if services are performed on tangible personal property that is exported before the service is made available in Canada (section 7, Schedule VI). ECG monitors supplied to licensed health institutions may further qualify as zero-rated medical devices under Part II of Schedule VI. The LP must retain evidence of physical export to a foreign consignee and, for calibration services, documentation that the instruments were shipped out of Canada prior to completion of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Export Declaration filed electronically via the Canadian Export Reporting System (G7) for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000 or for controlled goods
Commercial Invoice in English or French detailing HS 9018.19 ECG monitor product line, quantity, value, and foreign consignee
Bill of Lading (ocean, air waybill, or highway manifest) evidencing delivery to a destination outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire advice confirming payment from a non-resident buyer in foreign currency
CUSMA (or other applicable free trade agreement) Certificate of Origin if preferential customs treatment is sought at the destination port
Export Permit issued under the Export and Import Permits Act if the device or its embedded encryption modules appear on the Export Control List
Complete forwarding file, including pickup order, CBSA customs release, and foreign customs entry or delivery confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the reporting period; the limitation period is extended if a waiver is filed or is unlimited in cases of fraud or misrepresentation. Where export zero-rating is claimed without sufficient documentary proof, CRA will assess GST at 5% on the supply, disallow input tax credits associated with the invoice, and charge arrears interest. Gross negligence penalties under subsection 285.1(1) of the Excise Tax Act apply to false statements made knowingly or due to gross negligence, equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax understated. Failure to register or remit attracts an additional 6% penalty plus interest; failure to file the T5013 partnership information return triggers penalties of CAD 25 per partner per day to a maximum of CAD 2,500 per month. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day repatriation deadline; however, the 180-day benchmark is accepted by CRA as evidence of a genuine export sale. Unrepatriated receivables beyond this period may be recharacterized under transfer pricing rules in subsections 247(2)–247(3) as a deemed loan, taxable benefit, or deemed dividend to non-resident partners, with correlative Part XIII withholding obligations and possible adjustment penalties of 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return — annual federal income and partner-allocation filing for the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); each partner's share is separately reported on the partner's T1 or T2 return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 25 per day per SBN, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 per return, plus 10% gross-negligence penalties on unreported allocations; persistent non-filing can trigger a formal demand, criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act, and revocation of partnership income-allocation treatment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (annual-filer scheme) including medical device sales and zero-rated export reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); quarterly instalments are due when annual net tax exceeds CAD 3,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the net tax owing plus an additional 1% per complete month for up to 12 months; arrears interest at the prescribed CRA rate; continued defaults may result in an assessment, lien registration, and third-party demand against the general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) annual renewal under the Food and Drugs Act for Class I and multi-parameter monitoring devices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application must be received on or before the licence expiry date, which is the anniversary of original issuance; the renewal window opens 60 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of licence immediately prohibits importation, sale, and distribution of the monitor devices; continued commercial activity without a valid MDEL is an offence under the Food and Drugs Act and may result in seizure, injunction, compliance orders, and a full new-application review timeline upon reinstatement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Declaration / Annual Return (registration maintenance in the province of formation and each extra-provincial registration province)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Corporate Registry (filed through the registered corporate agent; federal jurisdiction is recognized for CRA and Health Canada matters only because no federal limited partnership registry exists)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the limited partnership's original registration; each extra-provincial registration is renewed on its separate anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fees of CAD 100–CAD 200 per registry, administrative cancellation of the LP registration after repeated non-filing, loss of standing to commence legal proceedings in that province, and potential joint and several liability exposure for the general partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No direct federal audit statute applies to a limited partnership; however, an independent audit becomes mandatory if (a) the LP or its general partner is a reporting issuer under provincial securities law, (b) the general partner is a CBCA corporation whose gross revenues exceed CAD 10 million or total assets exceed CAD 5 million, (c) the partnership agreement or lender covenant requires audited financial statements, or (d) Health Canada requests audited quality-system documentation as part of MDEL compliance review
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable partnerships and where financing covenants mandate IFRS; otherwise Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada Handbook Part II, with partner capital account presentation

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The federal beneficial-ownership register mandate currently applies to CBCA corporations and does not yet extend to limited partnerships; for the CA_LP, the general partner must annually confirm the 25%-or-greater partner interest schedule to the provincial LP registrar when the annual declaration is filed and must report any partner-interest change of 25% or more in the T5013 for the fiscal year in which the change occurs; identical UBO data must be retained on-site for CRA and financial-institution AML due-diligence inspection
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (contributions and capital schedule)
Register of General Partner (equivalent to directors' register with residency details)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, LP Agreement and consents)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 500–CAD 1,500 (USD 370–USD 1,110) per province per year; a second extra-provincial registration adds CAD 300–CAD 800 (USD 220–USD 590)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 15,000–CAD 35,000 (USD 11,100–USD 25,900) for a full audit of a mid-sized medical device partnership; CAD 6,000–CAD 12,000 (USD 4,400–USD 8,900) for a review engagement where no mandatory audit applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate (post General Rate Reduction); LP itself is fiscally transparent, so income is taxed at the partner level; combined federal plus provincial corporate rates approximate 26.5% in Ontario (11.5% provincial) and 27.95% in Quebec (12.95% provincial); federal rate rises to 19% for corporations with taxable capital employed in Canada exceeding CAD 50 million under Budget 2024 proposals.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Manufacturing and Processing (M&P) profits deduction under ITA s.125.1 preserves a reduced federal M&P rate of 15% for qualifying ECG monitor assembly/calibration; Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit of 35% refundable for CCPCs up to CAD 3,000,000 qualifying expenditures and 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs; Accelerated Investment Incentive allows 100% first-year CCA for qualifying clean-tech and manufacturing machinery (Class 43.2 and Class 53); provincial manufacturing and innovation tax credits, plus federal investment tax credits for green technology applicable to energy-efficient patient monitor production.
